title: Suncrest Medical SOC2/ISO27001 Posture Review
summary: Redwood (AE+SE) ran through Suncrest's security posture questions for SOC 2 and ISO 27001 readiness. Discussion covered how Redwood provides trust center access, control mappings, RBAC/SSO integration, audit log retention, and encryption/KMS options for hosted, dedicated, and private deployments. Action items: Redwood to share SOC 2 report and controls mapping, customer to return security questionnaire and request demo of Trust Center, schedule follow-up to review SAML metadata and test audit log export.

Priya Shah - Share controls mapping spreadsheet (SOC2 -> Redwood controls) by 2026-01-20

Schedule follow-up tech deep dive to demo audit log export and KMS integration week of 2026-01-25
action_items: Jesse Miller - Send SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 mapping - due 2026-01-18
Priya Shah - Export sample audit log and instructions for retention config - due 2026-01-21
Mark Rivera - Complete vendor security questionnaire and return - due 2026-01-22
transcript:
Header: 2026-01-15 15:00 PT | Duration: 46m | Attendees: Jesse (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Carla (CSM), Mark (CISO - Suncrest), Lena (Dir IT), Aaron (Compliance), Samir (Cloud Eng)

[00:00:00] Jesse: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jesse from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE, joining me is Priya our SE and Carla from customer success. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Mark: Hi thanks, good. we wanted to get into the SOC 2 and ISO posture, so we can finish our security review for procurement.
[00:00:22] Jesse: Perfect. quick agenda — trust center access & reports, controls mapping to ISO 27001 and SOC 2, RBAC/SSO and SAML, audit logs / retention, encryption and KMS, and then next steps. any additions?
[00:00:33] Lena: No, sounds good. timeline wise we need to close by end of month.
[00:00:37] Priya: Great, i'll start with how we provide artifacts. we host a Trust Center portal with the SOC 2 Type II report, ISO summary, pen test exec summary — customers get read-only access via SSO. we can also map controls by control IDs to our implementation.
[00:00:55] Aaron: When you say read-only access, is that a link we can share with the compliance team? or do you provide a bundle?
[00:01:03] Jesse: Both. typically we provide a link plus a one-off secure download for the report. if your legal needs a bundled package we can provide that under an NDA.
[00:01:12] Mark: ok and evidence / controls mapping — do you map SOC 2 criteria to specific Redwood processes? we need the mapping to our internal GRC tool.
[00:01:21] Priya: Yes, we have a controls mapping spreadsheet that maps SOC 2 CC and ISO 27001 clauses to Redwood policies, procedures, and artifacts (e.g., access control policy, change mgmt, incident response). i'll attach that. note: some of the artifact names in the mapping are internal doc ids, there may be small differences in naming.
[00:01:40] Samir: Is that mapping granular enough for an auditor? we need to show evidence traceability.
[00:01:46] Priya: It's intended for that yes — we include links to the Trust Center artifacts and for certain items we can provide redactions as needed. for deep dives we can schedule a walkthrough with our compliance team.
[00:01:58] Jesse: quick note on hosting modes — for hosted customers you get the trust center link and standard set of artifacts. for Dedicated/Private we can provide more detailed logs and can support deployment-specific attestations.
[00:02:10] Lena: Data residency — can we get EU-only storage? we have some PHI-ish data that must remain in-region.
[00:02:18] Priya: Yes, we support region pinning for data in our Dedicated and Private options and for hosted we have region controls in some cloud regions. if you need strict EU-only residency, Dedicated or Private is the safe bet.
[00:02:29] Mark: Encryption at rest — do you manage keys or can we bring our own KMS?
[00:02:35] Priya: We support both. by default Redwood manages KMS keys and rotates them, but for Dedicated and Private you can integrate with your KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, or customer HSM) and we support envelope encryption. for hosted we also offer a BYOK option for enterprise plans.
[00:02:52] Samir: Any MFA enforced for root admins? RBAC granularity?
[00:02:56] Jesse: Yes MFA on all Redwood console admin accounts, RBAC supports roles and custom roles, and audit logs capture admin actions.
[00:03:05] Priya: i'll add that our RBAC is enforced at token level and resource level — you can restrict model deployments, routes, and dev/test prod environments. we also support SCIM provisioning for large orgs.
[00:03:18] Aaron: SSO — we use SAML 2.0, ok to integrate?
[00:03:22] Priya: Yep SAML 2.0 works. for initial setup we need your IdP metadata, we can provide sample SP metadata. some customers prefer SCIM for user sync; SAML for auth.
[00:03:33] Mark: Audit logs — whats the retention and format? we need syslog delivery to our SIEM and immutable logs for 2 years.
[00:03:42] Priya: We have structured audit logs with ISO timestamps. hosted plan default retention is 90 days, can be extended for enterprise; Dedicated/Private you can configure retention and export. we support pushing logs to S3, syslog, or direct to your SIEM via connector. immutability we can support via write-once S3 buckets + object lock on Dedicated.
[00:04:05] Samir: Are request/response payloads redacted in logs by default? we can't have PHI in logs.
[00:04:11] Priya: By default we redact sensitive fields and we support configurable request/response scrubbing and prefix caching so full prompts aren't stored. for strict use cases, Private deployment keeps data entirely inside your VPC and we can disable some telemetry.
[00:04:27] Jesse: Also want to call out that we do prefix/KV cache caching for performance but that cache can be isolated to the customer and subject to retention policies.
[00:04:36] Lena: Incident response — how do you notify customers? SLA?
[00:04:40] Jesse: We have an incident response policy documented in the Trust Center; customers get security incident notifications via the console and email, and for enterprise contracts we offer scheduled post-incident reviews. SLA for security incidents varies with contract but we aim for timely notifications.
[00:04:54] Aaron: For SOC 2/ISO evidence, do you allow auditor access or a break-glass option?
[00:04:59] Priya: We can provide read-only auditor access to the Trust Center and for Dedicated setups we can set up auditor connectivity to logs. there is a process and NDA.
[00:05:09] Mark: Controls mapping — can you map to our control IDs? we have a custom set.
[00:05:14] Priya: We can provide a mapping CSV and you can merge it into your GRC. if you give us your control list, we can do an initial crosswalk.
[00:05:23] Samir: On the encryption side, is hardware-backed key material supported? HSM?
[00:05:28] Priya: Yes HSM-backed keys supported for Dedicated/Private; for hosted we use cloud KMS.
[00:05:33] Jesse: ok a few common questions i always get — backup retention, vulnerability scanning cadence, and pentest frequency. we run infra scanning regularly and a third-party pentest annually; we can share the summary.
[00:05:46] Priya: Also, for network isolation — Private offers full VPC peering and no public ingress, Dedicated can be isolated into private subnets.
[00:05:56] Mark: One item: our procurement needs a contract clause for data breach notification timelines — is 72 hours acceptable?
[00:06:02] Jesse: We can commit to 72-hour notification in enterprise contracts.
[00:06:06] Aaron: About the Trust Center link — is it SSO-protected or tokenized?
[00:06:10] Jesse: SSO-protected. we can also provide time-limited signed links if needed.
[00:06:16] Lena: Ok great. can you show an example of the controls mapping?
[00:06:20] Priya: i'll screen share in the follow-up; for now i'll summarize some entries: SOC 2 CC6 — access control mapped to our IAM policy and RBAC enforcement, evidence: access logs + IAM policy doc. ISO 27001 A.9 mapped similarly. sometimes artifact names are different, transcription note: internal doc names may look off.
[00:06:41] Jesse: any other blocker items from your side?
[00:06:44] Mark: two: we need SOC 2 Type II and the mapping, and we want to validate SAML integration in a test tenant.
[00:06:52] Jesse: understood, we'll action those.
[00:06:55] Samir: for test tenant, do you spin up ephemeral accounts? what about API keys and rotation?
[00:07:00] Priya: We can create a time-limited test tenant and issue scoped API keys; keys rotate and we recommend short TTLs and automated rotation.
[00:07:09] Lena: Is there an admin audit trail for configuration changes?
[00:07:12] Priya: yes admin config changes are logged and we provide change history per resource.
[00:07:18] Mark: ok from compliance perspective, once we have the artifacts we'll escalate to legal and procurement. expected decision timeline end of month.
[00:07:26] Jesse: makes sense. quick recaps — we'll send SOC 2 report and trust center link, controls mapping spreadsheet, sample audit log export and sketched KMS integration notes. we will also stand up a test tenant for SAML testing.
[00:07:39] Aaron: sounds good. thanks.
[00:07:41] Jesse: thanks everyone, next steps in the calendar.

Notes: transcription imperfect in places, speaker overlap occasionally. timestamps approximate and not exact. The conversation included common sales tradeoffs — hosted vs dedicated vs private for residency and encryption needs.
